title: kate-ui: build the tab rows
summary: tabs.rs builds one TabRow per view from Workspace::views_in_order, with the document name, the modified flag, and whether the view is active. The tab bar paints these rows. lib.rs declares the module.

lane.reason: A Cursor local agent on the owner Mac codes this packet. The file has no GPUI import, but kate-ui tests run in the rust (macos-15) job and the Mac lane owns crates/kate-ui.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: Create tabs.rs with the SPDX header for kate-ui. Add mod tabs; to lib.rs with #[cfg_attr(not(target_os = "macos"), allow(dead_code))] like files. tab_rows maps each view id to its document name, doc.history.is_modified(), and active == ws.active_view == Some(id). A view whose document is missing is skipped. The test module is #[cfg(all(test, target_os = "macos"))] because a Workspace needs kate_syntax::Theme, like files.rs. The test tab_rows_follow_the_view_order opens two untitled documents, types x in the first, and asserts two rows, the first modified and not active, the second active. Do not nest an if inside an if. When two arms return the same value, write one condition with ||. Add each new test at the end of the one test module of the file, before its closing brace; create that module when the file is new. Do not write a second mod tests. An item with no caller outside tests gets #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]; the packet that adds the caller removes it. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: tabs::tests::tab_rows_follow_the_view_order
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because tabs.rs does not exist. After the change the rows follow views_in_order with the modified and active flags.
